title: C197B — Starter motor connector
introduction:
I use this page like an ID card for the starter motor connector: identify the connector, match its cavity to the table, then follow the circuit information. A mysterious plastic plug is much less mysterious once it has a name and a job.

### Match the drawing to the row

The face drawing has a single marked cavity. I find that same cavity in the pin-assignment table and read across the row, keeping the circuit number, color, gauge and function together. The listed function is **RELAY - STARTER**. The harness information under the drawing helps me confirm which reference I’m reading before I go chasing the wrong damn plug.

### Know what each field is telling you

The connector identifier names this connection; the cavity label identifies its individual terminal position. **Circuit Number** identifies the circuit, while **Color** and **Gauge** record the listed wire information. **Used** and **Terminal Part Number** complete the row. I leave Gauge in the reference’s own notation because this sheet does not state a unit standard. A blank Qualifier field means there is no additional qualifier written here, not that every Mustang uses the same connector.

For an actual electrical check, I pair this reference with the matching wiring diagram and diagnostic procedure. This drawing does not specify a terminal-side versus wire-side view, physical access or expected test readings.
